question: Children who undergo splenectomy for hereditary spherocytosis or thalassaemia must receive pneumococcal, meningococcal, and Haemophilus influenzae type b vaccines before the procedure, and lifelong prophylactic penicillin to prevent overwhelming post-splenectomy infection.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Splenectomised children face overwhelming post-splenectomy infection from encapsulated bacteria. Vaccination against pneumococcus, meningococcus, and Hib plus long-term penicillin prophylaxis are mandatory precautions — these should be taught alongside any discussion of splenectomy indications.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The asplenic state removes the major filter for encapsulated organisms (Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis, Haemophilus influenzae type b). Pre-splenectomy vaccination (ideally ≥2 weeks before surgery) and post-splenectomy penicillin prophylaxis (until at least age 5, and for ≥2–5 years regardless of age) are mandatory to prevent overwhelming post-splenectomy infection (OPSI), which carries 50% mortality.
